flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about yourself and why early childhood education matters to you.
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q1 Attempt 1]
Um, so I've always had like an interest in working with children. I think it's because it stems from me being like the oldest child and always having to take care of my siblings. And, um, ever since I was little as well, like I've always like, um, been intrigued by like child psychology and how that like early childhood development and all that. Um, and I just recently got my associates in psychology, um, last year at the end of last year. And since I was 18, turning 21 soon, um, I've like all my jobs have been with children. Like I started off, you know, just babysitting, tutoring. Um, I was a soccer coach for a little bit. I did summer camps. And then once I was 18, I was, um, I became a behavioral therapist. And then soon after I became a registered behavioral technician with kiddos with, you know, disabilities and stuff. And, um, afterwards I like, cause I would do, um, the therapy sessions at home clinics and at school. And I really loved the school environment. So after I left the company, it was due to not having like enough, like sessions and like, I guess just like it was a scheduling, um, you know, just like schedule. It was like hard to like get hours and stuff because, you know, parents would cancel or sometimes like kids would from therapy, no longer needed the services. So I wanted to, um, get introduced and to get more like, you know, knowledge on like school settings. So I became a special education aid. And then I was also a teacher. Like I was a paraprofessional in like a classroom for like a student. So I was like, you know, like, I guess her aid, like the teacher's aid. And then recently I was, um, I worked with, um, a speech like speech pathologist and I really loved how they would conduct therapy. And, um, right now I'm taking communication classes so I could get an associates in communications as well. So that in two years I could get both bachelors for psychology and communications. And I'm still debating on whether I want to be, uh, speech pathologist in the future or a therapist. Like I'm just kind of depending, like it just kind of depends. But yeah, like I just love working with kids. It's always been a passion and I love to like gain like more experience in that setting.
